title: Property assessments, appeal deadlines and system costs
question: Which records establish a fiscal consequence and which figures measure workload or authority?
finding: Two state compliance findings, one court-reviewed appeal and a system overrun disclose different consequences. Current workload figures require hearing and waiver records before individual deadlines can be assessed.
how: Compare the signed state survey and response, both appeal judgments, the settlement ordinance, the adopted contract amendment and the Controller’s line-level payments.
limits: A settlement ceiling, aggregate caseload and projected change in taxable value each have different units and scopes.

rows.test: How did the City handle the cap for late welfare exemption claims?
rows.record: California reviewers found that San Francisco sometimes gave a full welfare exemption after a late filing and sometimes added $250 to the bill. The Assessor agreed the system did not calculate the partial exemptions properly.
rows.limit: Can the City show the corrected amount on each deidentified tax bill?

rows.test: Did the Assessor have the required claim and eligible costs for a seismic exclusion?
rows.record: State reviewers found several cases in which the Assessor excluded retrofit work from new-construction assessments without obtaining the required claim form or documentation.
rows.limit: Which cost certifications arrived from DBI and which were supplied directly?

rows.test: How did the planned launch, vendor contribution and payments for the assessment system compare?
rows.record: Phase 2 of the replacement assessment system went live in September 2025. A joint review attributed 92% of the delay to Sapient. Both the City and the vendor funded additional work.
rows.limit: Which outstanding deliverables passed acceptance, and did operational incident records trigger any service credits?

rows.test: What happened when assessment appeal hearings ran past the statutory deadline?
rows.record: A California appeals court ruled that San Francisco had to use the owners’ stated values for two tax years after its appeals board missed a statutory deadline. Other years had different outcomes.
rows.limit: How much of the five-matter settlement did the City actually pay, to whom and in which tax years?

rows.test: How many contemporary appeals were already open?
rows.record: The Assessor’s FY2026–27 and FY2027–28 budget submission describes 14,000 open assessment appeals and more than 25,000 reassessment assignments. These are different workloads.
rows.limit: The budget submission gives no individual filing dates, waivers or default rulings. Those records are needed to count matters past a legal deadline.

rows.test: Did every pending parcel appeal reduce the district’s tax revenue?
rows.record: A September 2025 draft Treasure Island financing study used June 11, 2025 appeal data. One FY2023–24 appeal was withdrawn. All six FY2024–25 appeals were still open at that date.
rows.limit: The study projected revenue exposure. It distinguished waivers, provisional reductions, withdrawal and final decisions. It also identified a temporary pandemic extension for certain earlier applications.

detail.t: State explanation of the two-year rule and exceptions
